finding.summary: The factory dispatches by model name: `overview if model == cfg.effective_overview_model and overview_llm is not else review_llm`. ReviewSession.create calls the factory once with config.model (review role) and once with config.effective_overview_model (overview role). When the test config does not set `overview_model`, effective_overview_model falls back to config.model (config.py: `return self.overview_model or self.model`), so both calls compare equal and BOTH roles receive the overview stub. A test calling make_session(config, llm=scripted_review_llm, overview_llm=overview_stub) with a default config silently wires the overview stub into the review stage: the scripted responder never runs, the review stage gets 'Overview.' instead of JSON, and tests fail confusingly — or worse, tests asserting the incomplete/parse-failure path pass vacuously for the wrong reason. Nothing in the docstring warns that config.overview_model must be set for distinct llm/overview_llm to work.
finding.fix: Don't dispatch on model-name equality, since the two roles are indistinguishable when overview_model is unset. Either (a) fail fast in make_session: `if overview_llm is not None and not config.overview_model: raise ValueError('overview_llm requires config.overview_model to be set')`, or (b) distinguish roles positionally — ReviewSession.create invokes the factory deterministically (review first, overview second), so use a call counter/flag, or build the two GuardedLLMs explicitly instead of routing through the shared factory.

label: false_positive
